holidays.name: National Rocky Road Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the glorious combination of chocolate ice cream, marshmallows, and nuts. Grab a scoop, a cone, or just a spoon and a pint, and dig in to this bumpy, lumpy treat.
holidays.origin: Rocky road ice cream is commonly credited to William Dreyer, who in 1929 or 1930 in Oakland, California, cut up walnuts and marshmallows with his partner's tin shears and added them to chocolate ice cream. The name was said to be a nod to the rocky economic times of the Great Depression.
holidays.funFact: Dreyer reportedly used his partner Joseph Edy's tin shears to cut up the marshmallows, and the flavor was a hit, soon becoming one of America's classic ice cream flavors.

holidays.name: National Leave the Office Early Day
holidays.description: An unofficial day when workers are encouraged to ditch the desk a little early and enjoy the start of summer. Think of it as a permission slip to escape the cubicle for sunshine, snacks, and fun.
holidays.origin: This is an informal, tongue-in-cheek observance that appears on lists of quirky holidays and is celebrated on or around the first Friday in June, and sometimes on June 2 specifically. It has no single known founder and has spread mainly through calendars and social media.
holidays.funFact: Studies on workplace productivity have repeatedly found that people tend to be less productive on summer Friday afternoons, so your boss might secretly agree with this holiday.

holidays.name: National Bubba Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the brothers, friends, and good ol' boys in your life known as Bubba. It's a friendly shout-out to this Southern nickname and everyone who answers to it.
holidays.origin: The word 'bubba' comes from the Southern U.S. alteration of 'brother,' as young children pronounced the word that way. The nickname has been used for generations, and the observance grew from the light-hearted tradition of honoring the name.
holidays.funFact: President Bill Clinton was famously nicknamed 'Bubba' in his home state of Arkansas, and the name was also made famous by Bubba Gump Shrimp from the movie Forrest Gump.

holidays.name: International Sex Workers' Day
holidays.description: An awareness day that highlights the rights, safety, and working conditions of sex workers around the world, and calls for an end to stigma and discrimination.
holidays.origin: The day commemorates June 2, 1975, when around 100 sex workers occupied the Saint-Nizier Church in Lyon, France, to protest police harassment and violence and the lack of protection. The protest sparked an international movement.
holidays.funFact: The occupation in Lyon lasted about a week before police stormed the church, but it inspired similar protests across France and is still marked by activist groups every year.

holidays.name: National Do-Nut Day Eve? Not Quite: National Rotisserie Chicken Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the humble, golden, spit-roasted bird that rescues dinner plans everywhere. Celebrate by picking up a rotisserie chicken and turning it into tacos, sandwiches, soup, or just eating it straight from the container.
holidays.origin: Rotisserie chicken day is a modern food observance that has been listed on June 2 in several holiday calendars, and it celebrates a cooking method that goes back centuries, using a rotating spit to cook meat evenly over a fire.
holidays.funFact: Costco sells more than 100 million rotisserie chickens a year, and has kept the price at $4.99 since 2009.
